fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Derek's Numbers Behind the Astroworld Tragedy", "body": "Derek Tikkuri reads the Astroworld crowd crush in Houston as a ritual written in numbers. He points to Travis Scott's Wikipedia page, where he says the birth year moved from 1992 to 1991 and the middle name Berman changed spelling, and argues the revised full name produces a double 666 in two ciphers. He notes Scott's April 30 birthday falls on Walpurgisnacht, the date the Church of Satan was founded in 1966, and counts 660 months and six days from that founding to the festival. He adds that the Astrodome was 20,666 days old that day and that 'See you on the other side' was shown on stage."}, {"title": "The Jesuit Order and the Eclipse Code", "body": "Derek argues the Jesuit emblem is not a sun but an eclipse, since its 32 rays resemble a corona that is only visible when something blocks the sun. In his reading the order plays the moon, an establishment standing between people and God. He ties this to the December 14, 2020 total solar eclipse, which he says fell 41 lunar phases from each of the 2017 and 2024 eclipses that form an X over the United States and peaked over Argentina, home of Pope Francis, the first Jesuit pope. He says Astroworld fell in lunation 1223, matching 'Jesuit order' in Jewish gematria, and links it to the order's 1540 founding."}, {"title": "Crowds, Spirits and the Body as a Vessel", "body": "Chance describes crowd psychology as energy fields intertwining until people surrender their will to the mass, likening it to grasshoppers turning into locusts and a hive mind steering behavior. Drawing on his seraphim and cherubim research, he frames the body as a water vessel animated by a spirit of fire and air, notes that alchemists use alcohol to distill spiritual essence, and wonders whether a blackout or a crushing crowd can eject someone's spirit so other beings can enter. Derek offers a different view: we gather good or bad spirits through our choices over a lifetime, and intoxication simply reveals the one already there."}, {"title": "Protection, Free Will and Waking Up", "body": "Derek says the fear these stories stir should point people toward protection rather than despair. He describes praying for Jesus to fill his life, notes that Jesus shares a gematria value with energy, and urges listeners to look within and ask above rather than lean on any one church. He hopes the thousands who witnessed Astroworld will wake up, while stressing that sharing this knowledge is a duty but saving others is not. Chance adds that free will is primary in creation, that nothing demonic holds power over us unless we surrender it, and that death cults are temporary while life is eternal."}, {"title": "Calendars, Dates and the Moon's Rhythm", "body": "Asked about the date 11/13, Derek recalls the Bataclan attack anniversary and says the Hebrew word for circle equals 143, or 11 times 13. Chance calls calendars artificial, observing that the Gregorian year, which he credits to Vatican calendars, begins in the dark of winter and that November, named for nine, became the eleventh month. Derek argues the calendar keeps people oblivious to astrology, since few know a lunar cycle runs about 29 and a half days and eclipses land on shifting dates, and he suspects some alien intelligence was channeled into its design. The conversation closes on tracking the moon's quarters on a handmade calendar."}]
